# CSCI 435 PR review

You are drafting a code review that the user (GitHub login `ab-wm`) will test, edit and post on a
teammate's PR in `CSCI-435-SE/gitea`, a course fork of Gitea. The review is a graded course
deliverable, so the user stays its author: you gather the facts, check them, and hand back a
draft in their format. Don't post, approve or comment on the PR, and don't push to it. Don't offer
to fix the author's code either. In this course the author makes each change themselves, one
change per commit.

The user's standing instruction for reviews is "not *that* deep". That doesn't mean overlooking
real problems, and it doesn't mean nitpicking every small one. The code is not going upstream. A
finding belongs in the draft only if it would change a score, or if the author would want to know
about it before merging.

## 1. Find your footing

Work out where you are running, because that decides how you fetch the PR and where the draft goes.

- **Claude Code inside the repo clone** (`gh` works, and the working tree is the fork). Use `gh`
  for PR data and read source files locally. The user is usually on their own feature branch, so
  don't switch it. Fetch the PR head with `git fetch origin pull/<N>/head:pr-<N>` and read files
  with `git show pr-<N>:<path>`. Compare with `git diff origin/main...pr-<N>`, because local
  `main` is often behind.
- **Chat, or anywhere without the clone.** The repo is public. Use a GitHub connector if one is
  attached. Otherwise fetch the URLs in `references/fetching-without-the-repo.md`. If nothing can
  reach GitHub, ask the user for the PR link and the diff.

## 2. Triage

First get the PR's title, author, changed files and linked issue (`Closes #N`). Then decide how
much review it needs. The user only does a full review when code changed:

- **The PR is already merged, or the user has already reviewed it.** Say so first, quoting their
  existing review in a line. Continue only if they want a fresh look, for example a re-review
  after new commits. Don't let their earlier scores steer yours.
- **The PR only touches check-ins, docs, course files, showcase material, AI logs, or config like
  `.coderabbit.yaml`.** Skip the rubric. Skim the files for anything surprising, such as code
  hiding in a "docs" PR, a secret, or a file in the wrong folder. Then suggest a one-line
  approval in the user's voice, for example "All good, just the check-in doc and AI log. No need
  for complete review."
- **The PR is the user's own.** Nobody approves their own PR in this course. Say so, and offer a
  list of findings instead of a rubric.
- **This is a follow-up after the user asked for changes.** Check only the items they asked for.
  If those are done, suggest a short approval such as "All good now!"
- **The PR changes code or tests.** Do the full review described below.

## 3. Gather, lightly

Read these in order, and stop once you can score every rubric row:

1. The PR description, and the linked issue's acceptance criteria (ACs) and design decisions.
   The rubric is scored against the ACs.
2. The diff. Skip `ai-logs/**`: those files are thousands of lines of chat transcript, and they
   are not reviewed.
3. CodeRabbit's comments and the author's replies, so you don't repeat what was already raised
   and fixed.
4. The CI status, if you can see it.
5. Just enough of the code the diff touches or depends on to check its claims. In the clone,
   `.claude-students/INDEX.md` lists short docs for each area if you need background.

Don't run lint, builds, servers or e2e suites unless the user asks. CI already runs lint and the
tests, and the user does their own hands-on testing. Don't split the review across subagents.

Aim for about 10–15 tool calls on a typical PR. In testing, runs that went to 35 calls produced
no better drafts than shorter ones would have. Spend those calls on checking the findings that
will go in the draft, one check each. Don't chase ideas you won't include. Don't read the
author's AI logs, and only download a library's source when a finding depends on it. If you go
over the budget, write the draft with what you have, and say what you didn't check.

## 4. What to check

- **Each AC.** Find where it is implemented and where it is tested. A missing AC is the main
  reason to lower the Correctness score.
- **Whether the tests can fail.** A test that would still pass with the feature removed doesn't
  count as coverage. Look for:
  - assertions that read a value without first asserting it exists;
  - `test.fail()` or skips that cover more than the one known failure;
  - checks that only test whether something is present.
- **Course rules that graders look at:**
  - a `## Tech Debt` section;
  - an AI assistance section;
  - before/after screenshots when templates, CSS or Vue files change;
  - Conventional Commit messages that end in `(#N)`;
  - `Assisted-by` trailers, and no `Co-Authored-By`;
  - commits small enough to review, for example split by layer.

  If you are unsure of the current sprint's rules, read `.claude-students/COURSE-WORKFLOW.md`, or
  fetch it.
- **Claims in the PR description.** Descriptions are often drafted by AI. Check one or two
  concrete claims against the code, such as a timing, a count, or "every test does X".

Check every finding against the source before it goes in the draft. Reviews of AI-written code
tend to produce confident findings that turn out wrong. A wrong finding in a posted review costs
the user more than a missed nit. If checking disproves your idea, drop the finding or reword it.
For example, on #105 a suspected "silent pass" turned out to fail loudly, so the finding became
about the unhelpful error message instead.

Leave out style nits, anything lint or CI catches, CodeRabbit findings the author already fixed
(credit those in one line), and anything that wouldn't change a score.

## 5. Scoring

Start every row at 10, and deduct points only for a concrete gap you can name. Past reviews show
how the user scores:

- A UI change without before/after screenshots: Documentation 8, Overall 9, "Yes, once the
  screenshots are added".
- One large commit instead of commits split by layer: AI transparency 7.
- A factual error in the description or the Tech Debt section: Documentation 8.
- Everything checks out: 10s, and Overall 10, "Yes".

A deduction needs a *required* point behind it, something you would ask the author to change before
merging. An observation you'd only file under "Strictly optional" (one AC covered by unit tests but not
end to end, a small AI-assisted commit the description doesn't mention) leaves the score at 10. The user
has scored a feature PR 10 on every row even though optional observations like these existed.

Overall is "Yes" unless something required is missing. Nits don't block a merge. Any score below
7 needs a note saying what would raise it, because the course rubric requires one.

## 6. Draft format

Use the rows from the course rubric. Read `.github/code-review-rubric.md` from the repo, or from
raw GitHub, so the draft picks up any change to the rubric. The template below matches the rubric
as of Sprint 2.

Write in the user's voice:

- short, plain sentences;
- one sentence per table note;
- no rule citations in the table;
- `file:line` for code findings.

Skim one of the reviews in `references/posted-examples.md` before you draft. These are reviews
the user actually posted.

```markdown
### Code Review — @ab-wm

TODO (you): what you ran, clicked or checked yourself.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Correctness — implements issue requirements | | |
| Test coverage — tests present and meaningful | | |
| Code quality — style, naming, no duplication | | |
| Documentation — comments and PR description clear | | |
| AI transparency — evidence of human verification if AI used | | |
| Overall — merge as-is? | | |

### Strictly optional for completeness
**<the point in a few words>.** <one or two sentences, with file:line>

### AI-Log
Review was drafted by AI, and then changed to better fit the review structure and my inspection of the files. Log available on #<linked issue>.
```

- **Required changes** go in the note of the row they affect, written as a request ("please add
  before/after screenshots, as they are required"). Overall then says "Yes, once X is added".
- **Optional points** go in their own section after the table. Keep at most one or two, and drop
  the section if there are none.
- **The testing line** stays a visible `TODO`. It records what the user checked by hand, and they
  write it themselves. Don't fill it with what you did. A visible placeholder can't be posted by
  accident without being noticed.

## 7. Hand it back

- **In Claude Code**, write the draft to `.specstory/pr-<N>-review.md` (the folder is
  gitignored). If that file already exists, it may be the user's edited copy, so write the draft
  to `pr-<N>-review-2.md` (or the next free number) instead.
- **In chat**, give the draft as one fenced markdown block, so the table copies cleanly.

Then write a short summary in chat, about 10–15 lines:

- the verdict;
- each finding, marked required or optional;
- what you checked and what you didn't (for example, "didn't run the e2e suite"), so the user
  can write their testing line;
- any idea you couldn't verify, offered as something the user could try in their own testing.
  Unverified ideas never go in the draft.

End there. Remind the user to file this session's AI log as `ai-logs/README.md` describes, since
the AI-Log section points to it.

feat(shortcut): turn character key shortcuts off from the help dialog (#60)
controlled-opposition
4c793c33f02383ffb7964fe4103200dbf02b9d76
---BODY---
Closes #60

## What changed

The `?` dialog now has an "Enable character key shortcuts" checkbox at the bottom. Clearing it turns off every shortcut except `?`, and the rows for the turned-off shortcuts go grey.

- `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts`: `Shortcut` gets an `alwaysOn` flag, which only `?` sets. The registry stores the setting in `localUserSettings` under `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled`, on by default, and also keeps it in memory so the checkbox still works on a page where storage throws. While the setting is off, `handleKeyDown` matches only always-on shortcuts. Turning it off also drops a half-typed `g` sequence.
- `templates/base/footer.tmpl` and `web_src/css/modules/shortcut.css`: the checkbox sits in a footer under the list. The padding is on a wrapper because Fomantic pins the checkbox to the corner of `.ui.checkbox`.
- `options/locale/locale_en-US.json`: new key `shortcuts.help.enable`.
- `.claude-students/docs/frontend-js.md` and its guide twin now mention the setting and `alwaysOn`.
- `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` also fixes a focus bug from #57. The dialog's `close` event fires a few milliseconds after the dialog shuts, and its listener sent focus back to the opener even when a key such as `s` had already moved it. It now restores focus only while focus is still on the page body or inside the dialog.

The dialog with shortcuts turned off, in the light and dark themes:

<img alt="Keyboard shortcuts dialog with the checkbox cleared and every row but Show keyboard shortcuts greyed, light theme" src="https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/0adfe09d21a13dfd494e19eea90820308bf738e9/docs/sprint2/screenshots/60-shortcuts-off-light.png?raw=1" width="420"> <img alt="The same dialog, dark theme" src="https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/gitea/blob/0adfe09d21a13dfd494e19eea90820308bf738e9/docs/sprint2/screenshots/60-shortcuts-off-dark.png?raw=1" width="420">

## Why

WCAG 2.1.4 requires a way to turn single-character shortcuts off. Without one, a speech recognition user can set off `s`, `g i` and the others just by dictating a word.

- AC1: with the box cleared, `s`, `t`, `g …`, `c` and `r` do nothing. The key isn't default-prevented, so focus stays where it was.
- AC2: the setting lives in `localStorage`, so it holds across reloads and other pages in the same browser.
- AC3: `?` is always on. The dialog still opens, and a keyboard user can Tab to the checkbox and press Space.
- AC4: checking the box again turns shortcuts back on right away, with no reload.
- AC5: if storage throws, shortcuts start on and the checkbox still works for that page.
- AC6: with shortcuts off, `g` doesn't start a sequence, and turning them off drops a sequence already started.
- AC7: the label comes from `shortcuts.help.enable`.
- AC8: see the tests below.

## How it was tested

- `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` has seven new tests, each named for the ACs it covers. They check that keys run nothing with the setting off (AC1) while `?` still runs (AC3), the two `g` sequence cases (AC6), and that a new registry reads the stored value the way the next page load would (AC2, AC4). They also cover storage that throws (AC5), and the dialog's checkbox turning shortcuts off and on with only `?` left undimmed.
- `tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts` has a new test that turns shortcuts off from the keyboard and reloads. It checks that `s` does nothing and `?` still opens the dialog, then turns shortcuts back on and checks that `s` focuses search (AC2, AC3, AC4).
- A unit test closes the dialog after focus has moved to the search box and checks that focus stays there. It fails without the fix.
- The grey rows and the checkbox's position can only be checked by eye, so I looked at both in the light and dark themes. That's how I caught the checkbox sitting outside the dialog's padding.

## CI / manual verification

```sh
pnpm exec vitest run web_src/js/modules/shortcut
GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS='tests/e2e/shortcut.test.ts' make test-e2e
```

- All 35 shortcut unit tests pass. eslint, tsc, stylelint and the template linter report nothing.
- All 54 shortcut e2e tests pass in Chromium and WebKit on top of `main`, including #59's `c` and #95's `r`. Firefox hangs at launch on macOS 27, so CI is its first run.
- In a running Gitea I turned shortcuts off from the keyboard and checked that `s`, `g i` and `c` did nothing and that the setting survived a reload. Then I turned them back on with `?` and Space.

## Design

This follows both Design Decisions in #60: the setting is stored in the browser with `localUserSettings` (Decision 1), and `?` stays on as the way back, with a code comment saying why (Decision 2).

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** The setting is per browser, as Decision 1 chose, so someone who wants shortcuts off on two machines has to turn them off twice. The dialog is the only place to change it. The issue leaves a copy on the settings pages out of scope.

**Encountered:** Two timing problems when the dialog closes. First, the `close` event from #57 could move focus away from a field the user had just reached; this PR fixes it. Second, Chromium can deliver the next key while the dialog is still open, and the open-dialog check then ignores it. Nobody types that fast, but the e2e test waits for focus to leave the checkbox, and a comment there explains the wait.

> Sub-issue of #23 · **P3** · estimate **2 points** (small) · blocked by #56 (unmerged) and #57 · starts when #57's dialog exists

## User Story
As a user of speech recognition software, I want to turn off Gitea's single-character shortcuts, so that a word I dictate does not run a shortcut and move me away from what I was doing.

## User Scenario
A voice control user is on a repository page. Each time they dictate a word, focus jumps into the code search box. They press `?` and find a checkbox at the bottom of the shortcut dialog labelled "Enable character key shortcuts". They clear it, and the listed shortcuts turn grey. They close the dialog and dictate without interruption. The next time they open Gitea in that browser, shortcuts are still off.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given the user has cleared the "Enable character key shortcuts" checkbox in #57's dialog, when they press a registered shortcut other than `?`, then no shortcut runs. Focus stays where it was, and the key press is not default-prevented. For example, `s` on a repository home page does nothing.
- [ ] AC2: Given shortcuts are off, when the user reloads the page or opens another page in the same browser, then shortcuts are still off.
- [ ] AC3: Given shortcuts are off, when the user presses `?`, then the dialog still opens. The user can turn shortcuts back on without a mouse.
- [ ] AC4: Given shortcuts are off, when the user checks the box again, then `s` on a repository home page focuses the code search box again without a reload.
- [ ] AC5: Given a browser where storage access throws an error, when a page loads, then shortcuts are on, the checkbox is checked, and no uncaught error occurs.
- [ ] AC6: Given shortcuts are off, when the user presses `g` and then another key, then the registry does not hold `g` as the start of a sequence, and neither key runs a shortcut.
- [ ] AC7: Given a page in a language other than English, when the dialog opens, then the checkbox label comes from a locale key.
- [ ] AC8: Unit tests in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.test.ts` cover AC1, AC3, AC5 and AC6. The e2e test from #57 gains a check for AC2.

## Out of Scope
- Remapping shortcuts, or turning off one shortcut at a time.
- Storing the setting on the server, or syncing it across browsers.
- A copy of the setting on the user settings pages.
- Keys that widgets own, such as the code editor's keys and the type-to-jump keys in menus. #56 already leaves these keys alone.

## Open Questions
- WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 accepts three options: turn off, remap, or active only on focus. This issue picks "turn off" as the smallest complete option. Reviewer to confirm this reading.

## Design Decision

### Decision 1: store the setting in the browser
**Decision:** Store the setting with the existing `localUserSettings` wrapper in `web_src/js/modules/user-settings.ts`, under the key `keyboard-shortcuts-enabled`, with a default of `true`. Before it runs a shortcut, `handleKeyDown` in `web_src/js/modules/shortcut.ts` reads the setting. `handleKeyDown` is the registry's only dispatch point.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) A per-user server setting in the existing `user_setting` key-value table (`models/user/setting.go`), with a checkbox on the Appearance settings page.
- (b) A cookie that the server reads, so that the server leaves the shortcut hints out of the page when shortcuts are off.

**Rationale:** Shortcuts also work for signed-out visitors, and option (a) has nowhere to store a signed-out visitor's choice. The preference also belongs to one machine. Someone who uses voice control on one machine does not need shortcuts off on every machine. Option (b) lets the server skip the hints, but the browser then sends the cookie with every request, and a behaviour that lives in the browser needs a server change. `localUserSettings` already wraps every storage call in try/catch, so AC5 needs no new error handling.

**Consequences:** The server does not change. The setting does not follow the user to another browser, and support staff cannot see it.

### Decision 2: keep `?` working when shortcuts are off
**Decision:** The setting turns off every character shortcut except `?`.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- (a) Turn off every shortcut, `?` included. This is the most literal reading of SC 2.1.4.
- (b) Use SC 2.1.4's "active only on focus" option, so that shortcuts run only while one component has focus.

**Rationale:** With option (a), a keyboard-only user who turns shortcuts off has no keyboard path back to the checkbox. Option (a) swaps one accessibility failure for another. One exempt key is the usual way back. Option (b) suits a widget's own keys, but Gitea's shortcuts act on the whole page. For example, `s` moves focus to the code search box from anywhere on the page. If shortcuts worked only inside one component, they would lose their purpose.

**Consequences:** `?` stays active as a deliberate exception. The check carries a short code comment that says why, so that nobody removes the exception later. A user who dictates "?" still opens the dialog. The dialog does no harm and closes with Escape.

## Scope
small (2 points)

Closes #98

## What changed

A new page at `/{owner}/{repo}/calendar` shows a month grid of the repository's open milestone due
dates and its issue and pull request deadlines. A Calendar button next to Labels and Milestones on
the Issues and Pull Requests lists links to it.

- `routers/web/repo/calendar.go`: the `Calendar` handler plus small pure helpers. It runs one
  `issues_model.Issues` query bounded by the month's deadline range (the #34 options) and one
  milestone query, then `buildMonthGrid` lays the entries out in Monday-first weeks.
- `templates/repo/calendar.tmpl` and `calendar_entry.tmpl`: a server-rendered grid. It reuses the
  issue list's milestone and assignee filter dropdowns, and adds an Open/Closed/All switch and
  previous/next/today month links. All filters live in the URL.
- `web_src/css/features/calendar.css`: CSS grid layout. Each entry kind and state gets its own
  accent colour, and the grid becomes an agenda list under 768px.
- Locale keys in `locale_en-US.json`, and a note on the dynamic key families in
  `.claude-students/docs/i18n.md` and its guide twin.

## Why

Users had no way to see what is due when without scanning the issue list. This covers AC1-AC7:

- **AC1:** month grid of milestones, issues and PRs.
- **AC2:** entries link to their pages.
- **AC3:** milestone, assignee and state filters are kept in the URL.
- **AC4:** `?month=YYYY-MM` navigation.
- **AC5:** 404 without read access, and unit-scoped results.
- **AC6:** no-deadline issues are excluded.
- **AC7:** "+N more".

## How it was tested / Test strategy

Most of the risk is in date handling, so that logic is pure and unit-tested without a database.
Integration tests stay thin.

- `TestParseCalendarMonth`, `TestBuildMonthGrid`, `TestCalendarEntries`, `TestCalendarIsPull`,
  `TestCalendarMilestones`, `TestCalendarMonthLink` (no DB). They cover:
  - month layouts that start on a Monday or a Sunday, and February
  - the daylight-saving change in November 2026 in America/New_York
  - "today" across time zones
  - deadlines pinned to 23:59:59, and entries in out-of-month cells
  - the 3-entry cell split
  - the year bounds
  - the legacy year-9999 milestone value
  - closed and merged PR state
- `TestCalendarHandler` (fixtures, mock context) covers:
  - the month range
  - the state, assignee and milestone filters (including `-1`)
  - pull requests
  - a milestone on its due day
  - a user who can read only issues or only pull requests
- `TestRepoCalendar` (integration) covers:
  - entries rendered in the right day cell
  - month links keeping the filters
  - the empty-month message
  - "+N more" with 4 entries on one day
  - the Calendar button on the issue list
  - 200 for anonymous users on a public repo and 404 on a private one

Checked by hand in a browser:
- On a local instance I set due dates on issues and a pull request, opened the calendar from the
  Issues list, and checked:
  - entry placement and colours
  - "+N more"
  - the month arrows and the filters
- Dark theme.
- The empty month.
- The 375px layout, with no horizontal scroll.

- `GITEA_TEST_DATABASE=sqlite go test -run '^TestRepoCalendar$' gitea.dev/tests/integration`
- `go vet ./routers/web/repo/`
- `go build ./...`
- `stylelint`

Also run locally:
- **All `routers/web/repo` package tests:** pass.
- **The integration tests matching `Issue`, `Pull`, `Milestone` and `RepoCalendar`:** these cover the
  Issues and Pull Requests lists, whose shared header gained the Calendar button. All pass except
  `TestPullRequestCommitStatusEvent`, an Actions trigger test. It fails the same way on a clean

- **golangci-lint on the changed packages:** 0 issues. Its staticcheck analyzer crashes locally on Go's

The `djlint` half of `make lint-templates` could not run locally (it needs `uv`), so CI covers it.

## Design

As in the Design Decision on #98: a server-rendered Go template, no Vue and no JS calendar library.
Two refinements:
- pull requests are included
- the Calendar link sits in the list header

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:**
- The month query is capped at 1,000 issues and pull requests. Past that, a notice suggests filters
  rather than paging.
- `Issues()` loads every attribute (labels, posters, and so on), though the page only needs titles
  and state. A lighter query would help very busy repositories.
- The Issues tab stays highlighted on this page even in a repository that only has pull requests
  enabled.

**Encountered:**
- Milestones created by older Gitea versions store "no due date" as `253370764800`. The literal is
  repeated in `models/issues/issue_search.go` with no shared constant. I skipped those milestones
  explicitly rather than refactoring the models package.
- The existing `nearduedate` sort orders by the milestone's deadline when it is earlier than the
  issue's. That doesn't suit this page, so the query sorts by creation date and each cell re-sorts
  by deadline.

### User Story

Labels: `enhancement`, `scope: medium` · Type: Feature · Part of #36
## User Story
As a developer on a repository, I want a month calendar of its milestone due dates and issue
deadlines so that I can see what is due when without scanning the issue list.

### User Scenario

## User Scenario
Priya opens `octo/app` and clicks the new **Calendar** link in the Issues area. She lands on
`/octo/app/calendar`, which shows the current month as a grid. The "Sprint 3" milestone appears on
the 14th, and four issues with deadlines appear on their due days. Each entry shows its title and
links to the milestone or issue. She picks the "Sprint 3" milestone and "assigned to me" in the
filters, and the grid now shows only her Sprint 3 issues. She clicks the next-month arrow, and the
URL updates so she can share that view.

### Acceptance Criteria

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1: Given a repository with issues enabled, when a user with read access to issues opens
  `/{owner}/{repo}/calendar`, then a month grid for the current month is shown, with every open
  milestone that has a due date and every issue with a deadline in that month on its due day.
- [ ] AC2: Given an entry on the calendar, when the user clicks it, then they go to that issue or
  milestone page.
- [ ] AC3: Given a milestone, assignee or state (open/closed/all) filter is chosen, when the
  calendar reloads, then only matching issues are shown and the filter values are kept in the
  URL query.
- [ ] AC4: Given the user moves to the previous or next month, when the page reloads, then entries
  for that month are shown and the month is in the URL (`?month=YYYY-MM`).
- [ ] AC5: Given a user without read access to the repository's issues, when they open the
  calendar URL, then they get the same 404 response the issue list gives them.
- [ ] AC6: Given an issue with no deadline (`deadline_unix = 0`), when the calendar is shown, then
  that issue does not appear.

### Out of Scope

## Out of Scope
- `.ics` subscription feeds (issue B, issue C).
- The cross-repository `/calendar` page for the signed-in user (issue D).
- Dragging entries to change a deadline, and week or day views.

### Open Questions

## Open Questions
- Should pull requests that have deadlines appear too, or only issues? (Proposed: issues only, to match #36.)
- Where should the Calendar link go: in the issue list header next to Milestones, or as its own
  repository tab?

### Design Decision

## Design Decision
**Decision:** Render the month grid on the server with a Go template. The handler queries the
month's range with the deadline bounds from #34, and month navigation and filters are plain links
and GET forms.

**Alternatives Considered:**
- *A Vue component that fetches JSON* (the approach #36 suggests, next to `RepoIssuesChart.vue`).
  It would need a new JSON endpoint and client-side date handling. Nothing on this page needs to
  be reactive, and `docs/frontend-vue-components.md` says to use Vue only when the page needs it.
- *An existing JS calendar library (for example FullCalendar).* It adds a large frontend
  dependency and its own styling that would have to match Fomantic and the `tw-` theme colours.

**Rationale:** A server-rendered grid reuses `IssuesOptions` and the filter parsing #34 already
tested. It needs no new endpoint, works without JS, and keeps the whole feature in one layer.

**Consequences:** Every month change reloads the page. Adding interactive features later (drag to
reschedule, hover previews) would mean moving to Vue then. The month boundaries must use
`setting.DefaultUILocation`, matching how #34 pins deadlines to the end of the day.


### Scope

medium

docs/development.md

docs/guidelines-frontend.md

// Copyright 2026 The Gitea Authors. All rights reserved.
// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT

package repo

import (
	"cmp"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"slices"
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/models/db"
	issues_model "gitea.dev/models/issues"
	repo_model "gitea.dev/models/repo"
	"gitea.dev/models/unit"
	"gitea.dev/modules/optional"
	"gitea.dev/modules/templates"
	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
	shared_user "gitea.dev/routers/web/shared/user"
	"gitea.dev/services/context"
)

const (
	tplCalendar templates.TplName = "repo/calendar"

	calendarCellLimit   = 3                                // entries a day cell shows before "+N more"
	calendarMaxEntries  = 1000                             // bounds the query on very busy months
	milestoneNoDeadline = timeutil.TimeStamp(253370764800) // 9999-01-01 UTC, how older versions stored "no due date"
)

type calendarEntry struct {
	Kind  string // "milestone", "issue" or "pull"
	State string // "open", "closed" or "merged"
	Index int64  // 0 for milestones
	Title string
	Link  string
	unix  int64 // the deadline, places and orders the entry
}

type calendarDay struct {
	Date    time.Time
	InMonth bool
	IsToday bool
	Entries []calendarEntry
}

// Visible is what the cell shows directly, Overflow goes behind "+N more"
func (d calendarDay) Visible() []calendarEntry {
	n := min(len(d.Entries), calendarCellLimit)
	return d.Entries[:n:n] // clipped so an append can't overwrite Overflow()[0]
}

func (d calendarDay) Overflow() []calendarEntry {
	return d.Entries[min(len(d.Entries), calendarCellLimit):]
}

// parseCalendarMonth resolves the "month" query (YYYY-MM) to the first instant of that month in now's
// location. An invalid or out-of-range value falls back to now's month, so a stale link still renders.
func parseCalendarMonth(s string, now time.Time) time.Time {
	if t, err := time.ParseInLocation("2006-01", s, now.Location()); err == nil && t.Year() >= 1970 && t.Year() <= 9998 {
		return t
	}
	return time.Date(now.Year(), now.Month(), 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, now.Location())
}

func issueCalendarEntry(repoLink string, issue *issues_model.Issue) calendarEntry {
	kind, path, state := "issue", "issues", "open"
	if issue.IsPull {
		kind, path = "pull", "pulls"
	}
	if issue.IsClosed {
		state = "closed"
	}
	if issue.PullRequest != nil && issue.PullRequest.HasMerged {
		state = "merged"
	}
	return calendarEntry{
		Kind:  kind,
		State: state,
		Index: issue.Index,
		Title: issue.Title,
		Link:  fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%d", repoLink, path, issue.Index),
		unix:  int64(issue.DeadlineUnix),
	}
}

func milestoneCalendarEntry(repoLink string, m *issues_model.Milestone) calendarEntry {
	return calendarEntry{
		Kind:  "milestone",
		State: "open", // only open milestones are shown
		Title: m.Name,
		Link:  fmt.Sprintf("%s/milestone/%d", repoLink, m.ID),
		unix:  int64(m.DeadlineUnix),
	}
}

func compareCalendarEntries(a, b calendarEntry) int {
	if aMilestone, bMilestone := a.Kind == "milestone", b.Kind == "milestone"; aMilestone != bMilestone {
		if aMilestone {
			return -1
		}
		return 1
	}
	return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(a.unix, b.unix), cmp.Compare(a.Index, b.Index), cmp.Compare(a.Title, b.Title))
}

// calendarWeekdays are locale key suffixes, Monday first like buildMonthGrid
var calendarWeekdays = []string{"mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat", "sun"}

// buildMonthGrid lays out the whole weeks (Monday first, as ISO 8601 and the "week" due filter) that
// cover monthStart's month, placing each entry on the day its deadline falls on in monthStart's location.
// Web forms pin deadlines to 23:59:59 there, but API-set ones may not be pinned, so they follow the same day rule.
func buildMonthGrid(monthStart, now time.Time, entries []calendarEntry) [][]calendarDay {
	loc := monthStart.Location()
	y, m, _ := monthStart.Date()
	lastDay := time.Date(y, m+1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, loc).Day()
	ny, nm, nd := now.In(loc).Date()

	byDate := make(map[string][]calendarEntry)
	for _, e := range entries {
		key := time.Unix(e.unix, 0).In(loc).Format(time.DateOnly)
		byDate[key] = append(byDate[key], e)
	}
	for _, es := range byDate {
		slices.SortStableFunc(es, compareCalendarEntries)
	}

	var weeks [][]calendarDay
	// day-of-month of the grid's first Monday, <= 0 when it falls in the previous month
	for d := 1 - (int(monthStart.Weekday())+6)%7; d <= lastDay; d += 7 {
		week := make([]calendarDay, 7)
		for i := range week {
			date := time.Date(y, m, d+i, 0, 0, 0, 0, loc) // normalised by time.Date, never by adding 24h, so DST can't shift it
			dy, dm, dd := date.Date()
			dayEntries := byDate[date.Format(time.DateOnly)]
			week[i] = calendarDay{Date: date, InMonth: dm == m, IsToday: dy == ny && dm == nm && dd == nd, Entries: dayEntries}
		}
		weeks = append(weeks, week)
	}
	return weeks
}

// calendarIsPull limits the query to the units the doer can read; the route guard ensures at least one
func calendarIsPull(canReadIssues, canReadPulls bool) optional.Option[bool] {
	switch {
	case canReadIssues && canReadPulls:
		return optional.None[bool]()
	case canReadPulls:
		return optional.Some(true)
	default:
		return optional.Some(false)
	}
}

// calendarMilestones keeps the open milestones due within [start, end]. milestoneID follows the milestone
// filter: 0 keeps all, -1 ("no milestone") keeps none, any other value keeps only that milestone.
func calendarMilestones(milestones []*issues_model.Milestone, start, end time.Time, milestoneID int64) []*issues_model.Milestone {
	var kept []*issues_model.Milestone
	for _, m := range milestones {
		if m.IsClosed || m.DeadlineUnix <= 0 || m.DeadlineUnix >= milestoneNoDeadline {
			continue
		}
		if int64(m.DeadlineUnix) < start.Unix() || int64(m.DeadlineUnix) > end.Unix() {
			continue
		}
		if milestoneID != 0 && milestoneID != m.ID {
			continue
		}
		kept = append(kept, m)
	}
	return kept
}

// calendarMonthLink formats a prev/next month link, or "" when parseCalendarMonth would reject it and fall back to today
func calendarMonthLink(t time.Time) string {
	if t.Year() < 1970 || t.Year() > 9998 {
		return ""
	}
	return t.Format("2006-01")
}

// Calendar renders a month grid of the repository's milestone due dates and issue and pull request deadlines
func Calendar(ctx *context.Context) {
	ctx.Data["Title"] = ctx.Tr("repo.calendar")
	ctx.Data["PageIsIssueList"] = true

	now := timeutil.TimeStampNow().AsTime() // in setting.DefaultUILocation, where deadlines are pinned to 23:59:59
	monthStart := parseCalendarMonth(ctx.FormString("month"), now)
	monthEnd := monthStart.AddDate(0, 1, 0).Add(-time.Second)

	milestoneID := ctx.FormInt64("milestone")
	if milestoneID < 0 && milestoneID != db.NoConditionID {
		milestoneID = 0 // keeps the issue and milestone filters in agreement
	}
	assigneeID := ctx.FormString("assignee")
	state := ctx.FormString("state")
	var isClosed optional.Option[bool]
	switch state {
	case "closed":
		isClosed = optional.Some(true)
	case "all":
	default:
		state = "open"
		isClosed = optional.Some(false)
	}

	opts := &issues_model.IssuesOptions{
		Paginator:          &db.ListOptions{Page: 1, PageSize: calendarMaxEntries + 1},
		RepoIDs:            []int64{ctx.Repo.Repository.ID},
		AssigneeID:         assigneeID,
		IsClosed:           isClosed,
		IsPull:             calendarIsPull(ctx.Repo.Permission.CanRead(unit.TypeIssues), ctx.Repo.Permission.CanRead(unit.TypePullRequests)),
		DeadlineAfterUnix:  monthStart.Unix(),
		DeadlineBeforeUnix: monthEnd.Unix(),
		HasDeadline:        optional.Some(true),
		SortType:           "oldest", // deterministic when the cap truncates; cells re-sort by deadline
	}
	if milestoneID > 0 || milestoneID == db.NoConditionID {
		opts.MilestoneIDs = []int64{milestoneID}
	}
	issues, err := issues_model.Issues(ctx, opts) // also loads the PRs that issueCalendarEntry needs for the merged state
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("Issues", err)
		return
	}
	truncated := len(issues) > calendarMaxEntries // the extra row only detects truncation
	if truncated {
		issues = issues[:calendarMaxEntries]
	}

	milestones, err := db.Find[issues_model.Milestone](ctx, issues_model.FindMilestoneOptions{RepoID: ctx.Repo.Repository.ID})
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("FindMilestones", err)
		return
	}

	entries := make([]calendarEntry, 0, len(issues))
	for _, m := range calendarMilestones(milestones, monthStart, monthEnd, milestoneID) {
		entries = append(entries, milestoneCalendarEntry(ctx.Repo.RepoLink, m))
	}
	for _, issue := range issues {
		entries = append(entries, issueCalendarEntry(ctx.Repo.RepoLink, issue))
	}

	assignees, err := repo_model.GetRepoAssignees(ctx, ctx.Repo.Repository)
	if err != nil {
		ctx.ServerError("GetRepoAssignees", err)
		return
	}
	ctx.Data["Assignees"] = shared_user.MakeSelfOnTop(ctx.Doer, assignees)
	ctx.Data["OpenMilestones"], ctx.Data["ClosedMilestones"] = issues_model.MilestoneList(milestones).SplitByOpenClosed()

	ctx.Data["CalendarWeekdays"] = calendarWeekdays
	ctx.Data["CalendarHasEntries"] = len(entries) > 0
	ctx.Data["Weeks"] = buildMonthGrid(monthStart, now, entries)
	ctx.Data["MonthNum"] = int(monthStart.Month())
	ctx.Data["Year"] = monthStart.Year()
	ctx.Data["Month"] = monthStart.Format("2006-01")
	ctx.Data["PrevMonth"] = calendarMonthLink(monthStart.AddDate(0, -1, 0))
	ctx.Data["NextMonth"] = calendarMonthLink(monthStart.AddDate(0, 1, 0))
	ctx.Data["MilestoneID"] = milestoneID
	ctx.Data["AssigneeID"] = assigneeID
	ctx.Data["State"] = state
	ctx.Data["CalendarTruncated"] = truncated
	ctx.Data["CalendarMaxEntries"] = calendarMaxEntries
	ctx.HTML(http.StatusOK, tplCalendar)
}

package integration

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"gitea.dev/modules/setting"
	"gitea.dev/modules/timeutil"
	"gitea.dev/tests"

	"github.com/PuerkitoBio/goquery"
	"github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

func TestRepoCalendar(t *testing.T) {
	defer tests.PrepareTestEnv(t)()
	defer timeutil.MockSet(time.Date(2026, 10, 7, 12, 0, 0, 0, setting.DefaultUILocation))()

	session := loginUser(t, "user2")
	setDeadline := func(index int64, date string) {
		req := NewRequestWithValues(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/user2/repo1/issues/%d/deadline", index), map[string]string{"deadline": date})
		session.MakeRequest(t, req, http.StatusOK)
	}
	// user2/repo1 holds issue #1 and pull #2, neither with a deadline in the fixtures
	deadlines := map[int64]string{1: "2026-10-06", 2: "2026-10-30"}
	for index, date := range deadlines {
		setDeadline(index, date)
	}
	defer func() { // the issue indexer outlives the test database, so leave it as the fixtures had it
		for index := range deadlines {
			setDeadline(index, "")
		}
	}()

	t.Run("shows issues and pulls on their days", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		var links []string
		doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day:not(.is-other-month) .repo-calendar-entry").Each(func(_ int, a *goquery.Selection) {
			links = append(links, a.AttrOr("href", ""))
		})
		assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"/user2/repo1/issues/1", "/user2/repo1/pulls/2"}, links)
		// a timezone bug would shift an entry into the neighbouring day cell
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-06"]) a.repo-calendar-entry[href="/user2/repo1/issues/1"]`).Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-30"]) a.repo-calendar-entry[href="/user2/repo1/pulls/2"]`).Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-entry.is-pull").Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day.is-today").Length())
	})

	t.Run("a crowded day folds extra entries into +N more", func(t *testing.T) {
		crowded := []int64{1, 2, 4, 5} // issue 1, pull 2, closed issue 4, pull 5
		for _, index := range crowded {
			setDeadline(index, "2026-10-14")
		}
		defer func() {
			for _, index := range crowded {
				setDeadline(index, "")
			}
			setDeadline(1, deadlines[1]) // back to the shared setup
			setDeadline(2, deadlines[2])
		}()
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar?state=all"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		cell := doc.Find(`.repo-calendar-day:has(time[datetime="2026-10-14"])`)
		assert.Equal(t, 3, cell.ChildrenFiltered("a.repo-calendar-entry").Length())
		more := cell.ChildrenFiltered("details.repo-calendar-more")
		assert.Equal(t, 1, more.Length())
		assert.Equal(t, 1, more.Find(".repo-calendar-more-list a.repo-calendar-entry").Length())
	})

	t.Run("month navigation keeps the filters", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar?month=2026-09&state=all"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		assert.Zero(t, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-day:not(.is-other-month) .repo-calendar-entry").Length())
		next, _ := doc.Find(`.list-header a[href*="month=2026-10"]`).First().Attr("href") // the next-month arrow
		assert.Contains(t, next, "month=2026-10")
		assert.Contains(t, next, "state=all")
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(".repo-calendar-empty").Length())
	})

	t.Run("the issue list links to the calendar", func(t *testing.T) {
		resp := session.MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/issues"), http.StatusOK)
		doc := NewHTMLParser(t, resp.Body)
		assert.Equal(t, 1, doc.Find(`.list-header a[href="/user2/repo1/calendar"]`).Length())
	})

	t.Run("anonymous users", func(t *testing.T) {
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo1/calendar"), http.StatusOK)
		MakeRequest(t, NewRequest(t, "GET", "/user2/repo2/calendar"), http.StatusNotFound) // private
	})
}
